text: Avebury is a British mythological site. The great stone circles at Avebury have been associated with the Druids for centuries, but this link is not historical. The stones date from thousands of years before the Celts arrived in Britain. When the Celts reached what is now north Wiltshire, they found a huge ditch-encircled site already standing. The ditch has four openings, one at each of the four cardinal directions. Great stones stand upright within the circle. A double line of stones runs like sentinels along a pathway toward a nearby hill. Some evidence suggests the Celts adapted the site to their own ritual purposes. The similar monument of Stonehenge was adapted in the same way. Avebury was not built by the Celts. The pre-Celtic people of the Megalithic Civilization raised the stones. The site is so large that a whole village has grown up within its boundaries.

okr.objective: This article establishes Avebury as a prehistoric British site of great stone circles, later associated with the Druids but built by the pre-Celtic Megalithic Civilization.
